pageCache.pageTitle: Firs Farm Primary School - Vision and Values
pageCache.text:
Vision and Values
Our Vision and Values are central to everything we do at Firs Farm. Please take time to read them to understand where we are going (vision) and what we expect of children, families and adults in school (values).
Our Values inform key parts of the school including our behaviour systems, teaching ethos and celebration of children's achievements.
Our Values Assembly are termly assemblies where children who consistently demonstrate a value (and go above and beyond in most cases) are rewarded. Families are invited to share this with their children.
VISION: WHERE WE ARE GOING AS A SCHOOL
Children at Firs Farm thrive academically and emotionally in a supportive and welcoming environment. We celebrate difference and make sure children are proud of their own and each other’s heritage. We develop global citizens ready for the challenge of the future in the international city that is London. Our curriculum is designed so that children are the best they can be and strive for excellence. By providing opportunities to perform, take part in sports and experiences beyond the classroom we equip children with independence, resilience and teamwork.
VALUES: WE EXPECT ALL CHILDREN,
FAMILIES & STAFF TO UPHOLD THESE

Welcome
A warm welcome to Firs Farm Primary School. I am very privileged to be the Head Teacher of such a vibrant and successful school.
We are a large inclusive community and our school is built on the belief that all children have the right to reach their potential and the right to an excellent education. The Staff at Firs Farm work tirelessly to ensure that this ethos is put into action.
We have an established House system that all children engage with and are a Unicef Rights Respecting School.
Children also have the opportunity to develop as citizens through various other groups such as Junior Travel Ambassadors, the school council and playground rangers.
Our parents are part of the life of the school and our PTA organises a range of events from Pamper Nights to Summer Fayres. Our school is fortunate to be sited beside the Firs Farm Wetlands and have its own extensive grounds.
On this website you will find more details on our curriculum, school life and statutory information such as KS2 SATs as well as our school policies. If you would like to come and visit please make an appointment at our school office (either in person or by contacting us on office@firsfarm.enfield.sch.uk). If you have any questions that the website cannot answer then please email office@firsfarm.enfield.sch.uk

Congratulations Firs Farm!
National Fitness Day 2024
This year, Firs Farm celebrated another incredible National Fitness Day. We understand the importance of how leading a healthy, active lifestyle isn't just for the day, but for life. We took part in the National Fitness Day initiative 10@10 whereby the whole school completed an Active Mile! All children from Reception to Year 6 got out and moving - this could have been skipping, singing, dancing, jogging, running or even hopping round the playground! We also had many other activities throughout the day such as a fitness bingo, brain breaks and yoga. Some children even made videos at home talking about what their favourite sport is and gave you an insight on how to play it. Check out the videos and pictures below!

Physical Education is a crucial part of the curriculum at Firs Farm. Each week, children participate in 2 allocated hours of PE, both indoors and outdoors. Every year, we receive a set amount of money dedicated for Sports and PE. Below are our impact statements for this amount and how we used the money last year, in addition to how we intend to use it this year.
Sports Day 2023
Sports Day 2023 was a great success! With boundless energy, enthusiasm and a true sense of sportsmanship, our students from Key Stage 2 on the 27th June and Reception/Key Stage 1 on the 13th July, showcased their talents, perseverance, and teamwork. We kicked off the day with a "Chariots of Fire" Parade, cheering on our house teams! Following this, we completed a range of multisport activities ranging from Javelin, Sack Race, Egg and Spoon, Stepping Stones and many more! Sports Day ended with a fantastic line up of competitive races from all year groups...even some parents and teachers too!
Both Sports Days were filled with excitement, friendly competition, and memorable moments that truly embodied the spirit of our school community. Our dedicated team of teachers and staff worked tirelessly to organise a variety of engaging activities, ensuring that every child had an opportunity to shine and enjoy the day to the fullest.
None of this would have been possible without the invaluable support and encouragement from our dedicated parents and guardians. Thank you for cheering on our young athletes, ensuring they arrived on time, and for being their biggest fans. Your presence and enthusiasm elevated the atmosphere and made the events even more special for our children.
We must also extend our appreciation to the PTA for funding some of the new equipment that was used this year. Their commitment to promoting physical fitness, teamwork, and fair play has undoubtedly left a lasting impact on our students.
Year 4 Bikeability Course
Bikeability is the nationally recognised cycle training programme that is accessible to all children. It’s about acquiring the practical skills to cycle safely and with confidence on today’s roads. For children to participate in school Bikeability training, they must have basic riding skills (without stabilisers). There are three Bikeability levels. Year 4 completed Level 1 which is designed to give children control over their bike and takes place in groups in a space away from traffic such as a playground or closed car park. Year 4 thoroughly enjoyed the experience and were pleased when receiving their badge and certificate at the end! You can visit the Cycle Confident website at www.cycleconfident.com for details.

Remote Learning Provision
REMOTE LEARNING PROVISION
Please see the document below detailing our Remote Learning Provision. This provision would be used should the school have to close due to weather conditions, for public health reasons (an outbreak that meant a local or national response) or other reasons that mean the school cannot operationally open but can provide lessons on line.
Our Online platform is Teams. Children are put into class Teams at the start of the academic year and class teachers and staff use these to set homework and communicate with families. Each child has a Teams account using their school email which gives them access to MS Office. This is used for live and recorded lessons when we use remote learning.
Full details of our provision is in the document below.

SCHOOL TRIPS KS2
In KS2 children have many opportunities to have new experiences out of class including residential stays. We believe children benefit from these opportunities in many ways including working collaboratively as teams or in paired work, developing their independence and resilience in being away from home. They also have lots of fun!
We have the following events:
YEAR 3: SLEEPOVER IN THE SCHOOL! One night sleep-over in the school hall during the Summer Term. Children have a light snack, games, songs and even a campfire before bedding down for the night.

Admissions
Admissions governance and policies for schools | Enfield Council
If you would like your child to attend our school, please see full details of our admission arrangements below. if you would like a tour of the school please contact the school office to arrange one. During the Autumn Term there are scheduled tours for parents interested in Reception places the following year. Please contact the office for more information or view the calendar which will give times/dates.
An in-year admission is when you need to make an application to a school outside of the normal admissions round for the start of Reception.
Please refer to the information at www.enfield.gov.uk/admissions. Applications are made through the online application form on this site. Pupil’s starting our school in the middle of a year will have an introductory meeting with a member of the Headship team. Parents are required to visit our school with their child as part of the admissions process. All new admissions are supported to ensure they are felt welcomed and make friends easily by having a set of friends in class responsible for them. They will be monitored daily by a member of the Senior Leadership Team
If you apply for a place at Firs Farm but are unsuccessful, you are able to appeal to the Local Authority who will hear your case.
Appeals should be lodged 20 days after you receive notification of a refusal. The LA will hear an appeal within 30 days of the appeal being lodged.
To lodge an appeal and for further details please go to the link below. The PDF on appealing is also available below.
There are separate arrangements for children with SEND and/or ECHPs. Please contact the SEND department for further details.

pageCache.text:
Mixing and rebalancing classes
RE-BALANCING/MIXING CLASSES
At Firs Farm, we re-balance classes at the end of Reception, Year 2 and Year 4. This allows an opportunity to mix the classes to ensure we have a balance of abilities and gender. It also allows us an opportunity to look at class dynamics and ensure they are effective.
We mix these year groups as these are at the end of key stages/curriculum and allow classes to be at their most effective when they start the new key stage.
We will start this process during the second half of the Summer Term. Children will be asked to pick friends that they would like to have in their new class and, once we have this information, class teachers and senior leaders balance the classes. They use information on children's ability and progress in class alongside other information. We will tell children and parents/carers towards the end of the Summer term when we will also have transition activities before we break up.
Below you can find documents that will provide further detail including the research that supports us.
Please find links to the forms for 2025-26 for the current Reception, Year 2 and Year 4 classes.

RHSE & PSHE SEPT 2026
From September 2026 schools have to introduce a new PSHE (personal, social, health & economic) and RSHE (relationships, sex, health education). Much of this is now statutory, which means schools have to teach it – we are allowed to decide when to teach topics. Below is a summary of what how we propose to deliver the RSHE curriculum. Further details on the PSHE curriculum can be found on the menu on the right.
PDFs of the information below and the full proposed policy can be found at the bottom of this page.
The school and governors would like to hear the views of staff and parent/carers. They will take these views into account when they meet to confirm the new policy and curriculum (July 2026).
Below you will find a summary of the new curriculum and RSHE policy, full versions of the proposed PSHE and RSHE policy and a link to the Parent/carer questionnaire.
Please take time to read all the information and respond. Following the launch in September we will have regular briefings so that families know when different topics are being taught. The curriculum for Early Years (Nursery & Reception) has not changed.
Please respond using our form Parent/Carer PSHE/RSHE curriculum form – Fill in form . If you would like a paper copy please either download the PDF and return via the school office or request a paper copy from the school office.
